conviction_note: Event confirmed for 2026-10-28 15:30 JST (close-to-close window). The release is very likely to ADD a second full-year raise: Q1 Adj. operating profit was already 20.9% of the raised plan against roughly 17.6% at the same point last year, and Hitachi raised at Q2 in both FY24 and FY25. But that raise is the market's base case: the one aggregator found puts street FY EPS about 7% above the company guide, and in Oct 2024 a raise below the street drew -5.4%. So findings sum to +0.5 and p_up is only 54. abs_move is 5.5, Hitachi's own Q2 reactions (-5.4, +7.2) and the 5.77 proxy, with MSFT/GOOGL results, the FOMC and GE Vernova's print all inside the window adding noise but no direction. Scaled number (2*0.54-1)*5.5 = +0.44.

findings.finding: Q1 FY27/3 Adj. operating profit of 294.3bn yen was 20.9% of the already-raised 1,408bn full-year plan. Last year Q1 was about 17.6% and H1 about 42% of the final year. Hitachi raised the full year at Q2 in FY24 and FY25 and again at Q3 FY25 and Q1 FY26. So a second FY raise at this print is likely; the question is its size against a street that already sits above the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Raise at Q2 FY24 (2024-10-30), judged below the street's 923bn Adj. OP: -5.38% next close. Raise at Q2 FY25 (2025-10-30, NI 7,100->7,500bn): +7.15%. Raise at Q1 FY26 (2026-07-29, EBITA +100bn): +6.01%. New-year guide 2026-04-27: -5.77% (closes from Yahoo 6501.T daily bars).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The aggregator's FY EPS of ~216 yen against the guide's 201 means the street already expects a raise, and the stock is +14% since the Q1 print. What is not priced is the size: a raise to ~950bn NI or more would clear it. A raise of only the Q1-H1 beat, or one held back for Middle East/FX caution (as in Oct 2024), would not. If the market expected a bigger raise, the pre-print 5-day tape would not be negative and the margin long would have built, not slipped from 8.66 to 7.16.
findings.independence: Q2 FY25 short-term article confirming the Q2-raise habit: https://s.kabutan.jp/stocks/6501/news/k202510300126/ (2025-10-30). Same company documents, so this is one fact, not two.

findings.finding: ABB's Q3 (published 2026-10-20) showed record orders, +40% comparable to $12.06B, with data-centre orders up triple digits and the electrification orders driving it, and nudged its FY revenue guide up. That is direct read-through to Hitachi Energy's grid/transformer order intake, Hitachi's largest profit engine, in the same quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ABB itself fell about 5% on the print (ABBN.SW 74.7 -> 71.0 on 10/20), so this sector is currently selling strong orders. Hitachi rose 10/20-10/21 (+1.2%) and then fell 4.4% on 10/23 with the AI complex.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it has been public for six sessions and ABB's own holders sold it. What is left is that Hitachi's Energy orders and backlog land on the print, and that print comes after a two-week AI/grid de-rating (GEV -18% and Siemens Energy -16% from early October). Strong Energy orders could look like relief rather than confirmation. A proxy, so sized small.
findings.independence: Same-week context from kabutan/MINKABU on the AI-complex selloff and rebound: https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=6501&b=n202610271043 (2026-10-27). That source is about positioning, not orders, so it is independent of ABB's numbers but does not confirm Hitachi's orders.

findings.finding: The yen has firmed against the Q2-Q4 plan rates: USD/JPY 157.9 and EUR/JPY 175.6 on 10/28 against 160 and 185 assumed (Q2 averages were 159.3 and 183.2). Re-basing H2 at spot costs only about 5bn yen of Adj. EBITA on Hitachi's stated sensitivities (12bn per yen USD and 6bn per yen EUR over Q2-Q4), so it trims any raise slightly.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to an FX re-base at Hitachi; the sensitivity is small (about 0.4% of FY EBITA).
findings.why_not_priced: FX is public and the effect is arithmetic, so this is near zero by construction. It is filed because it decides whether the H2 raise is a little smaller than the H1 beat.
findings.independence: Yahoo FX series JPY=X / EURJPY=X (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/EURJPY=X?range=6mo&interval=1d), retrieved 2026-10-28.

findings.finding: In July Hitachi built a Middle East risk of only -10bn yen Adj. EBITA into Q2-Q4, after Q1's hit of -7bn came in well below the -20bn it had assumed. Since then WTI has climbed from about $85 at the Q1 print to about $100-103 through September and October. The conflict has escalated after the assumption was set, so the release may widen the risk allowance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY26 said the Middle East impact was 'below the initial assumption' and the stock rose 6.0%. There is no instance of a widened allowance to measure.
findings.why_not_priced: Oil is public, so the macro is priced. The transmission to Hitachi is inference, and 10bn yen is under 1% of FY EBITA. A larger allowance would also offset part of any raise in finding 1 rather than stand alone.
findings.independence: WTI weekly series CL=F (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/CL=F?range=6mo&interval=1wk); Nikkei on Middle East disruption hitting manufacturers' hiring (https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXZQOUC1301M0T11C26A0000000/).

rejected_candidates.detail: A non-consolidated J-GAAP item; under IFRS consolidated (the reporting basis in the 短信), equity-security sale gains do not run through profit, so it does not bear on the consolidated print.

baseline_tension: Mild positive against a mildly negative priced lean (-0.625, margin-overhang driven) and a negative 5-day tape. The strongest positive the release could carry, a second FY raise above the street, was looked for and is the base case, which is exactly why it is mostly priced. The strongest negative, a cautious raise below the street as in Oct 2024 (-5.4%), is equally plausible, so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: nothing changed: rule 1 (negatives resting on a public series move p_up toward 50) applies to the FX and oil findings, but both were already sized at -0.1/-0.2 and carried almost no weight in p_up 54; rule 2 (negatives outnumbering positives) does not bite (two positives, two small negatives), and the strongest positive (a raise above the street) is written in baseline_tension.
